headline: Intel & AMD ACE CPU Extensions boost AI on x86 chips
summary: New instruction set makes matrix multiplication more power- and density-efficient, enabling better AI task performance on CPUs.
details: Intel and AMD have jointly released the full specification for their new ACE CPU extensions. This standard leverages existing AVX10 registers but adds dedicated silicon for matrix multiplication, aiming to improve AI task efficiency on x86 processors.

The key benefits of ACE include enhanced power efficiency, simplified development and optimization, and the ability to utilize AVX's 512-bit inputs for easier integration with current designs. This is crucial as matrix multiplication is fundamental to AI workloads.

ACE instructions can perform up to 16 times more operations per input vector compared to AVX10. While actual speedup varies by implementation, this advancement promises better performance and reduced overhead for AI tasks running on CPUs, especially when GPUs are unavailable or insufficient.

A significant advantage of ACE is its implementation-agnostic nature. This means ML frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow can use a single code path, eliminating the need for multiple variations tailored to different hardware and AVX support levels.

ACE natively supports a wide range of data types used in ML, including INT8, INT32, FP8, FP16, FP32, and BF16, as well as Open Compute Project's MX block-scaled formats. This offers developers a consistent target across x86 hardware and allows for quicker execution of NPU-specific workloads on CPUs when needed.
